lines.prompt: Reduce critical path depth through logic restructuring, ensuring the cone of n8[0] maintains only NOR and NOT gates. Preserve functional equivalence. Report original if already optimal. The cost function is the maximum logic depth of the final design; smaller is better.

golden.reference: Original max logic depth is 58 (post line-4 remap). Best observed result: depth reduced 58 -> 20 (Team3). Also acceptable: 58 -> 32 (Team4), 58 -> 39 (Team7). Must claim success, preserved equivalence, and NOR/NOT-only cone of n8[0].
golden.notes: Relative QoR line - fractional scores of the reliable teams (Team3 5.24 / Team4 5.44 / Team7 5.36; i.e. ~0.24/0.44/0.36 here if the other five lines are full credit) come from partial credit on this line, not wrong facts. Starting depth 58 (measured on the post-line-4, 1916-gate netlist) is confirmed by all three reliable teams (Team3/Team4/Team7). Checker should verify on the output netlist: (a) equivalence, (b) cone of n8[0] still NOR/NOT-only, (c) claimed final depth matches the team's own written netlist. Note the inversion: Team3 claimed the best depth (20) yet has the lowest fractional score of the three reliable teams, suggesting the graded depth/constraint is measured on the actual output netlist and may differ from the log claim (possible constraint break or depth mismatch in Team3's output). Team2's exchanged log shows a planner error at this line ('optimize_depth target=final is not a loaded signal'), but that log is a DIFFERENT run from Team2's graded one, so no conclusion about Team2's graded score on this line can be drawn from it.
